description:
As Pakistan tries to position itself as a peace broker and diplomatic power in the Middle East, it faces violence and political turmoil at home. 

Regional elections in Pakistan-administered Kashmir have been marred by deadly clashes between protestors and security forces. A banned activist movement - the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) - called the protests to oppose the practice of reserving 12 legislative seats for candidates from India-administered Kashmir. 

Meanwhile, an attack on a police checkpoint in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, near the Afghanistan border, has reportedly killed at least 11 officers. No one has claimed responsibility for the attack. There has been a recent surge in violence along the border in recent months, as security forces battle the Pakistan Taliban or TTP.

description:
European football's governing body, UEFA, says all its member countries would boycott future World Cup tournaments -
over Fifa President Gianni Infantino's controversial proposal to sell stakes in the competition to private equity investors.

The lead investor would be a venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner - the brother of Jared Kushner, US President Donald Trump's son-in-law.

Infantino has offered billions of dollars in payouts to global football federations to support his plan. Uefa is accusing Fifa of using football "to enrich themselves and their friends." 

And now, CONCACAF, the football governing body for North and Central America and the Caribbean, is also rejecting Fifa's plan. 

In a statement, it says, 'the membership expressed deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal, the artificially short deadline imposed, and the absence of any review or approval by the relevant FIFA governance bodies.'

The US military said it has completed a "heavy wave" of strikes against Iran in retaliation for Tuesday's attempted ballistic missile attacks on American forces.
 
Iran has responded by continuing attacks across the region. Jordan said it shot down five Iranian missiles, while Kuwait reports one person was killed in an Iranian strike.
 
The conflict is now pulling in more countries. This week saw the first publicly announced joint US-Saudi strikes against Iranian proxies in Iraq. Egypt has also blamed a drone attack for a fire on two ships, marking the first time it has been targeted since the war began five months ago.
 
With more countries being drawn in and diplomacy struggling to gain traction, are fears of a wider regional war becoming reality?
 
On the Iran War Today, we bring you up to date with everything you need to know about the conflict and what might come next.

description:
The Democrats almost certainly need to win the US Senate race in Michigan if they are to take control of Congress in November’s midterm elections but picking a candidate is exposing a stark choice for the party. 

Next week party members in the state will decide between a left wing candidate backed by Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and a centrist candidate backed by establishment Democrats like Gretchen Whitmer. It's opened up a debate about whether the success of other progressive candidates like Zohran Mamdani could be replicated across the country as the Democrats build a strategy to take on the Republicans at the midterms and beyond. 

Just how important is the race in Michigan for the Democrats, and will the outcome have an outsized role in deciding how they approach the 2028 presidential election?

description:
Uefa's 55 member associations have voted to boycott World Cups if Fifa proceeds with its plan to sell stakes in its competitions to private investors.
 
The decision was made at an emergency meeting called to discuss the proposals announced by Fifa - world football's governing body - on Tuesday.
 
Uefa, which governs European football, had made its opposition clear by releasing two damning statements about the plans - and that strength of feeling has now been reaffirmed.
 
The boycott would cover all Fifa competitions, including the men's and women's World Cups and Club World Cup, and be triggered if Fifa president Gianni Infantino's proposals are voted through by member associations.

In Spain, 24,000 people have been told they can return to their homes in the Madrid region, but some fires further afield have continued to burn.
 
Fire crews in France have been tackling wildfires in the south-west as temperatures soar to 40C, prompting fears more fires could break out.
 
Officials in the Gironde region insist fires there are under control. Thousands of evacuees can now return to their homes but they’ve been warned they may need to leave again.
